B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Cloudinary’s pricing page includes access to MCP servers in the Free plan. It does not state a separate MCP charge. Some asset-generation features consume Image Generation credits.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: The pricing page lists Free at $0, Plus at $99/month, and Advanced at $249/month on monthly billing; annual billing shows $89/month and $224/month respectively. The Free tier lists 25 monthly credits; Plus 225; Advanced 600.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Cloudinary plans include monthly credits and feature entitlements. The Asset Management tool reference says each image generation uses Image Generation credits. Pricing page values may vary by billing period and plan.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Remote servers use OAuth by default, with API-key headers documented as an alternative for most servers. Cloudinary documents optional region and tool-selection headers for the Asset Management server. The supplied endpoint’s own access conditions are unknown.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and end user; organization administrators may also control Cloudinary account settings and permissions.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: No official list was found for the exact input host. Best available official list: https://asset-management.mcp.cloudinary.com/ lists 30 tools. actions.json contains those 30, followed by 2 names found only in Claude’s connector directory (publisher-verification label shown on that directory); these are not confirmed for the input host. The official Cloudinary overview describes five specialized servers but does not give a combined tool total. Glama’s Cloudinary overview is a server-directory listing, not a per-endpoint complete tool list. Claude lists 21 names on its Asset Management connector page; 19 names overlap the official 30 after normalizing none of the names, while download-asset and asset-public_id-rename are catalogue-only. Official tool names and counts take precedence.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Cloudinary recommends disabling unnecessary servers/tools, enabling header embedding for request/rate-limit metadata, and using CLI/SDK for large or bulk uploads. These are documented setup/workflow recommendations; no evidence shows the supplied server enforces them.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The official upload tool description says uploaded files are stored with backup and revision history. The hosted reference documents asset-level access-control options. Cloudinary’s privacy policy distinguishes personal information it controls from uploaded content processed under its Data Processing Agreement where applicable. These statements do not establish MCP-specific retention, AI training, or logging controls.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Cloudinary describes remote servers as OAuth-authenticated by default and says the user can select the product environment during login. It also documents optional API credentials for remote servers where supported.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The available documentation describes configuration and feature behavior but the supplied endpoint could not be matched to the documented Asset Management host. Consequently, enforcement of the documented OAuth, permission, backup, and access-control behavior on the supplied host is unverified.

contradictions: Input endpoint https://mcp.cloudinary.com/mcp is not the documented Asset Management endpoint. The supplied endpoint test returned 403 and the prepared evidence files recorded HTTP 404 for GET requests to the host/path, while Cloudinary’s official documentation and endpoint page identify https://asset-management.mcp.cloudinary.com/mcp. The 30 documented tools are therefore best-available evidence for a related official server, not verified tools of the exact input host.

Claude’s connector directory lists download-asset and asset-public_id-rename, which do not appear in the official 30-tool Asset Management list. They are retained after the official tools in actions.json as third-party, unconfirmed names.

The supplied endpoint returned HTTP 403 without a WWW-Authenticate header; all four supplied well-known OAuth metadata URLs returned HTTP 404. Cloudinary documents OAuth for its named remote servers, but the endpoint’s own metadata does not corroborate that behavior.
observations_for_research: Cloudinary publishes several specialized MCP endpoints, permitting capability separation by product area.
The documented Asset Management server offers a configurable tool-selection header and configurable response-header collection, exposing context-selection and operational metadata choices to clients.
Image-generation tools distinguish temporary output from managed-asset storage, and the reference describes a fallback to temporary output when upload permission is absent.
